idiom_name: descriptor class instance (Breed) + const pointer/reference from each Monster, registry in std::unordered_map
implementation_notes: C++ already compiles the mechanism in for code-defined types - the vtable is a type object and every polymorphic instance carries its pointer - so the pattern's remaining job is making the type set data instead of code. The local idiom is an ordinary class or struct for the descriptor (shared data plus, where behaviour varies, std::function slots or virtual member functions) and a const pointer or reference member in the instance class, with a factory method on the descriptor so construction has one path. Descriptors loaded from JSON or config are registered in a std::unordered_map<std::string, Breed>; the line of code saved compared with a hand-written hierarchy is small, but the type set moves out of the build. Keep the classic class hierarchy when the kinds are closed, when each kind has genuinely different behaviour, or when compile-time exhaustiveness matters.
pitfalls: Holding a const Breed& (or Breed*) requires the registry to outlive every instance; if types can be reloaded or replaced, own them with std::shared_ptr<const Breed> instead.

Storing behaviour as std::function or raw function pointers inside the descriptor re-implements a vtable by hand - slower and easier to get wrong than virtual functions or a strategy object when behaviour really differs per type.
Mutating a registered Breed in place retroactively changes every existing Monster; treat descriptors as immutable and derive a new Breed for a tuned variant.
